transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... honestly, I'm mainly here because HR at work and, well, my sister, they keep saying I've gotten too thin. My weight has kept dropping since my divorce, which I guess they're a little worried about. But from my side, I just see that my suits fit a lot sharper now. Being a sales rep, looking put-together is really important, right? 

I don't really see it as a huge problem, but I wanted to do the right thing and get it checked out like they asked, just to be safe. Does that... does that make sense for why I'd come in?
Have you been intentionally eating less or avoiding certain foods to lose weight or stay thin?

Um, well, I wouldn't really say I'm avoiding food just to... just to be thin. It's more about staying sharp and efficient for work, you know? Like, most days I just keep it to coffee in the morning. It's quick and gets me going. And then maybe I'll grab a protein bar between sales calls if I need a little boost. Then at night, I try to make healthy choices, so I'll do something small, like just some grilled chicken, usually without the rice or anything heavy like that. 

I just... well, to be completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound bad, but... if I actually sit down and eat a big, full meal, it kind of feels like I just messed up the whole day? Like I lost all my momentum and ruined my progress. I'm sure a lot of busy guys in sales eat on the go like that, right? I hope that answers what you were asking.
Do you judge yourself mainly based on your weight or body shape?

Um... I guess maybe a little bit? But I think that's pretty normal, isn't it? I mean, especially in my line of work, presentation is everything. 

I just... well, when I look in the mirror before a big meeting or, you know, if I'm getting ready for a date, I do tend to... I guess I kind of zero in on my stomach and my face. And if I feel like I look a little soft, or maybe not as lean as I should be, I just get this awful feeling that people are going to look at me and think I'm sloppy. Or weak, you know? Like I don't have the discipline to handle their accounts. 

I don't want to sound vain or anything. It's just really important to me to project the right image. That makes sense, doesn't it? I'm sure you see a lot of guys who want to look their best for their careers.
Would you say that your weight or shape has a strong impact on how you feel about yourself overall?

Um... well, I wouldn't say it has a really *strong* impact on everything. Like, it's definitely not the only thing that matters to me, if that's what you mean. 

I still feel really good about myself when I hit my sales quotas, or, you know, when I'm just being a good brother to my sister. I guess... I guess staying lean just helps me feel like I have things under control? Especially after the divorce, it's just been really nice to have one area of my life that feels completely sorted out and disciplined. 

But I definitely don't want you to think I'm, like, obsessed with it or that my whole self-esteem crashes if I'm not perfect. I just like to maintain a good, professional baseline. I hope I'm explaining that right... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
After eating, do you ever make yourself exercise a lot, use laxatives, or do anything else to try to burn off the calories or keep from gaining weight?

Um, no, I don't really do anything like that. I mean, I definitely don't use laxatives or... or make myself sick or anything extreme like that. That sounds really unhealthy, and I try to be pretty careful about my body. 

I do go to the gym, of course, but just a normal amount, I think? Like, if I have a bigger dinner with a client, maybe I'll just push a little harder on the treadmill the next morning, but that's just basic fitness, right? Just trying to balance things out. I'm definitely not punishing myself or anything. I just want to stay in good shape. That's pretty standard for guys my age, isn't it?
Have you ever felt out of control when eating, or eaten a lot in a short amount of time, like more than most people would eat in the same situation?

Um, no, definitely not. I've never really felt out of control like that. I actually try to be pretty mindful about what I eat, so I don't really do the whole... bingeing thing, I guess you'd call it? 

Sometimes if I'm at a really good restaurant or a holiday thing, I might have an extra piece of bread or something, but I think that's pretty normal, right? I mean, I definitely don't eat huge amounts all at once. I just try to keep things reasonable and steady. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for... I just don't really struggle with that particular issue.
Have you ever gone for long periods without eating, or followed very strict diet rules to control your weight?

Um, well... I wouldn't call it "very strict rules," exactly. I think it's more just... having a routine that works for me? Being on the road for sales, you know, it's just easier to keep things simple. 

Like, most days I'll just stick to coffee in the morning to get going, and then maybe grab a protein bar between calls if I need it. And then for dinner, I usually just do something small and clean, like some grilled chicken, but I'll skip the rice or potatoes. 

It's just... I don't know, I feel like if I sit down and eat a big, heavy meal in the middle of the day, it just throws me off. It kind of feels like I messed up my momentum for the whole day, if that makes sense? So I just prefer to keep it light. That's just being efficient, right? I mean, a lot of busy guys eat like that, don't they?
Would you say that your feelings about yourself are often tied up with how you feel about your body weight or shape?

Um, well... I mean, I guess everybody cares about how they look, right? Especially in my line of work. You have to look sharp if you want people to take you seriously. 

But... yeah, I suppose it does affect me a bit. Like, when I'm getting ready in the morning, looking in the mirror before a big pitch or... or even just going on a date, I definitely check things out. I tend to focus right in on my stomach or my jawline. And if I feel like I'm looking a little... soft, I guess... it just really gets in my head. 

I start worrying that people are going to look at me and think I'm lazy, or sloppy, or just... weak, you know? Like I don't have the discipline to take care of myself. And then it's hard to feel confident for the rest of the day. But that's just normal professional pressure, isn't it? Wanting to present well? I hope I'm explaining that right... I just want to make sure I'm making a good impression on people.
Have your concerns about your weight or shape ever interfered with your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it interferes, exactly. I mean, I'm still hitting my numbers at work, managing my whole route just fine. I make sure I get the job done, you know? 

But... I guess maybe it has changed things a little bit socially? Like, with client dinners or... or going on dates. I just find it's a lot easier if I can kind of control the menu, or know exactly where we're going ahead of time. And if I can't do that, I... well, I might just make an excuse and turn the invitation down. 

It just feels safer to keep to myself sometimes, rather than deal with the stress of a big restaurant meal where I don't know how things are cooked. But I'm still working hard and doing my job! It's just a little adjustment I make to keep things running smoothly. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound too anti-social.
Have you ever been told that your weight was too low or that you needed to gain weight, and if so, how did you respond to that suggestion?

Um, well... yeah, I guess people have brought it up. Like, my family mostly, and maybe a couple of the guys at the office. They... they kind of make a big deal about my weight sometimes, saying I look too thin or that I need to put on some pounds. 

But... I don't know, I just try to reassure them that I'm completely fine. Because I am, really! I mean, I still jog every morning, I'm out there working my entire territory, and I'm hitting all my sales numbers. I have plenty of energy to get everything done. So when they say stuff like that, it just... it doesn't feel like some kind of medical emergency to me, you know? 

I'm just staying lean and active to do my job well. I just try to explain that to them so they won't stress out. I hope that's an okay way to handle it? I just really don't want people worrying about me or thinking I'm sick when I'm actually functioning perfectly fine. Does that sound reasonable to you?
Have you ever avoided social situations or felt extremely anxious in settings where food is involved because of your concerns about weight or shape?

Um, well, like I mentioned a little bit before... I guess it does happen sometimes. I mean, I still manage my whole sales route perfectly, so it's not like it's ruining my life or anything. 

But... yeah, if there's a client dinner or... or a date, and I don't have a say in where we're going or what's on the menu... I do get a little anxious. It just feels easier to avoid it altogether. So I have been turning down more invitations lately, and just kind of keeping to myself. 

It's not that I don't want to be around people! It's just... I like to know what I'm eating, so I can stay on track, you know? It just feels more responsible that way. I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult or anything... I'm just trying to be careful. Is it normal to want to have that kind of control over things?
Have your concerns about your weight or shape ever caused problems in your personal relationships, like with friends, family, or romantic partners?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it causes actual *problems*, no. Not really. I mean, like I mentioned earlier, my family brings it up sometimes, but we don't argue about it or anything. I always try to keep things peaceful with them and just reassure them that I'm doing great. 

And as for romantic partners... well, I guess I haven't really been dating much lately, just because the whole restaurant thing gets a little complicated. So there isn't really anyone to have conflict with in that department right now. 

With my friends, they're pretty understanding, I think. I might miss out on a few get-togethers or happy hours after work, but I always make sure to text them and stay in touch so they know I still care. I really try my best not to let my routine bother anyone else. It's just my own personal way of doing things, so I'd hate for it to ruin a relationship. I just really want to be a good friend and a good son, you know? I hope I'm still doing okay in that regard... does that sound like a normal way to handle it?
Have your concerns about weight or shape ever caused you to withdraw from people or activities that were once important to you, even if it wasn't a formal social event?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still do all the things that really matter, like my job and keeping up with my family. I guess maybe I don't go to the gym with my buddies as much as I used to, but that's just because I prefer to run on my own now. It's just more efficient that way, you know? 

I haven't really stopped doing anything I care about. I just... I guess I just like my routine. It's working for me, and I feel like I'm managing everything pretty well. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm totally isolating myself or anything like that, because I'm definitely not. I'm still out there every day doing my job. That's a good thing, right?
Have you ever felt distressed or upset specifically because of your concerns about your weight or shape, even when other people might not see a problem?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I get really distressed or upset. Not in a bad way, at least. I mean, sure, sometimes I might feel a little frustrated if I feel like I'm not making progress, or if I notice my clothes fitting a little differently. But I think that's pretty normal, isn't it? Everyone wants to look their best and stay healthy. 

I don't let it get to me too much. If I feel a little off about my shape, I just try to focus on being disciplined and sticking to my routine, and that usually makes me feel better. I try to stay positive about it. I'm not, like, crying in front of the mirror or letting it ruin my day. I just want to make sure I'm staying on top of things. That's a healthy way to look at it, don't you think? I'm just trying to be proactive.
Have your concerns about your weight or shape ever caused you significant emotional distress, even when you're able to maintain your routine and appear in control?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I experience significant emotional distress. I mean, sure, like anyone, I might get a little anxious if I feel like I'm losing control of my routine, but it's really nothing major. It's just a fleeting thought, you know? 

I think because my routine is so structured, it actually keeps me from getting distressed. It gives me a sense of order. So, I don't really have those moments where I feel completely overwhelmed or upset about my weight. I just focus on my goals and keep moving forward. I'm really trying to handle it in a balanced way... I hope that comes across? I just don't want you to worry that I'm secretly falling apart or something, because I'm honestly doing okay. That makes sense, right?
Do you currently see yourself as being normal weight, underweight, or overweight, even though others may tell you that you're too thin?

Um, well, I guess I'd say I see myself as pretty normal. I mean, I know my family and some people at work have been making a big deal about my weight lately, saying I'm too thin, but... I don't really see it that way. 

I'm still jogging every day, I'm out there working my territory, and I'm hitting all my sales numbers. If I were really, you know, dangerously underweight, I wouldn't have the energy to do all that, right? So it just doesn't feel like some big medical emergency to me. I feel like I'm functioning perfectly fine. I just like staying lean and active. That's a reasonable way to look at it, isn't it? I just don't want anyone to think I'm not taking care of myself, because I really am.
Do you currently see yourself as being underweight, even though others have told you that you look too thin?

Um, no, I... I really don't see myself that way. I know we sort of just touched on this, and I'm definitely not trying to be difficult or brush off what you're asking, I promise. It's just... when I look in the mirror, I really don't see this frail, underweight person that my family seems to be so worried about. 

I just see a guy who is staying lean and keeping in shape. I mean, I feel like I look fine, honestly. I hope it's okay that I'm being completely honest with you about how I see things? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right answers, but I just don't see myself as being underweight at all.
Even though others have told you they are concerned about your thinness, do you still feel that you are at a healthy weight and not underweight?

Um, yeah, I do. I really do feel like I'm at a healthy weight. I know we keep circling back to this, and I hope I'm not frustrating you... I really want to be cooperative. It's just that, honestly, I feel healthy. 

I mean, I'm active, I'm doing my job well, I feel strong when I'm out on my runs. If I were actually unhealthy or too thin, I wouldn't be able to keep up with my life the way I do, right? I just think my family is maybe being a little overprotective. I really hope you can see where I'm coming from. I'm just trying to stay fit, and I feel like I'm doing a pretty good job of it... is it okay that I feel that way?
